newsitem.title: PAKISTAN: Pakistan Telecom chief sparks optimism.
newsitem.headline: Pakistan Telecom chief sparks optimism.

text.p: Pakistani analysts said on Monday that investors should snap up shares of state-run Pakistan Telecommunication Co Ltd on the basis of restructuring plans and expected higher earnings.
They were speaking after a meeting with new PTCL chairman Naseem Mirza on Saturday in which he briefed the investment analysts about future strategies.
ING Baring Securities in its daily preview issued a buy recommendation following the briefing, saying the company was very attractive at current levels.

Kalim Aziz, head of research at Barings, quoted Mirza as saying PTCL had revenues of 19 billion rupees ($472.4 million) and a net profit of 8.9 billion rupees in the first half of fiscal 1995/96 (July-June).

"The management gave indications of eight to nine billion rupees (profits) for the second half, bringing total fiscal 1995/96 earnings to 16.9 billion to 17 billion rupees, or an earning per share of 3.3 to 3.5 rupees," Aziz said.

Nadeem Naqvi, analyst at International Asset Management Co Ltd (IAMC), said implementation of plans described by Mirza would certainly turn around investor sentiment and lift PTCL's currently depressed share price.

"If Mirza is given the freedom to exercise his power and make the required changes, he can put the company on the critical path to privatisation backed by a significant rise in earnings growth within the next two to three years," Naqvi said.
Analysts said Mirza planned to halt a decline in return on equity by effective and efficient cost controls and proper marketing.
He also intended to lower financial charges through better liquidity management and internal generation of funds for capacity expansion.
Naqvi said PTCL planned to raise the monthly line rent by 50 to 100 rupees and add a second pulse every five minutes on local calls.
He said PTCL could improve its cash flow by better recovery of arrears. "Mirza said PTCL can unlock more than eight billion rupees by clearing out the defaults," he said.

Naqvi said most foreign investors in PTCL including his own firm, an affiliate of Morgan Stanley Asset Management Inc, were interested in the capacity expansion plans of PTCL keeping in view the low penetration ratio per capita.

He said that by June 1998 the number of installed lines was expected to be 3.63 to 3.65 million lines and PTCL planned to increase its lines to 5.18 million, in addition to another 300,000 to 400,000 lines dedicated to electronic mail and the Internet, by June 2003.
The company also plans to increase capacity utilisation to 85 percent from 70 percent now by aggressive marketing.
Naqvi said the general feeling was that if the plans are implemented PTCL earnings could grow 15 to 20 percent annually over the next three years.
He said shares were currently very attractive and he hoped the government would let Mirza implement his programme in 1997 and go for privatisation by early 1998.
"A better-managed PTCL is likely to attract a major international communication player with a view to placing the Pakistan network in its global strategy," Naqvi said.
Analyst Abid Naqvi of Taurus Securities said: "PTCL can see a significant performance improvement and a consequent increase in shareholder value."
PTCL shares closed 0.30 rupees up at 27 rupees at the Karachi Stock Exchange on Monday. ($1 = 40.22 rupees)
